text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will invest in the holding of the Szczecin shipyard the Hipolit Cegielski (HCP) ship engine maker and the Gdynia yard, the Polish EBRD branch president Allan Pillaux said. The bank's investment will reach $100 million, PAP news agency quoted an unnamed source as saying.

- Seven prospective investors have expressed interest in acquiring stakes in the Romet bicycle plant in Bydgoszcz, western Poland, slated for privatisation this year. An 80 percent stake will be sold, 15 percent will pass to the plant's employees and a five percent stake will be kept by the state treasury as a privatisation reserve.

- Poland's tax office assigned 17.441 million tax identification numbers to taxpayers by the end of February this year, the finance ministry taxation supervision department deputy director Tadeusz Zajm said.

- Poland's average gross monthly salary in the corporate sector was 1,073 zlotys in March, showing a 4.7 percent increase compared with February and a 21.4 percent increase compared with the same period last year, GUS said.

- The Ampli electrical engineering equipment trader in Tarnow, southeastern Poland, will present a share issue prospectus to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) this week. The company is planning a share issue worth 3 million zlotys.

- The IBCA rating agency considers decreasing the long-term and short-term ratings of the Polish Investment Bank (PBI) to be sold to Kredyt Bank in Warsaw by the National Bank of Poland, the central bank. When owned by the central bank PBI boasted a BBB long-term and short-term rating.

- Global Finance monthly named Britain's Citibank as the best bank operating on emerging markets. Holland's ING bank was named the markets' leader and Bank Rozwoju Exportu was selected Poland's best locally operating bank.

- Poland's KGHM Polska Miedz copper conglomerate is the world's top silver producer with an annual output of 933 tonnes of silver, which represents 6.3 percent of global production, KGHM's spokesman Piotr Bielowski said.
- Fiat Auto Poland earned a net profit of $108 million last year and Skoda Poland, controlled by Volkswagen, made a net profit of $5.7 million in 1996, the companies said.
- Poland has formed a Credit Insurance and Insurance Guarantee Commitee to assess export contract insurance applications.

- LOT Ground Services of Poland's national air carrier will go on strike if negotiations related to a 40 percent salary increase and work conditions improvement bring no positive results, the Solidarity trade union's representative Andrzej Pielak said.

- The listed Mostostal Gdansk construction firm is planning to increase the share capital from 6.5 million zlotys to 10 million zlotys through a C-series share issue of 2.6 million shares nominally worth 2.5 zlotys per share, the company said.
